messages:
michael: Heads up — we got a customer report that EventSource clients are receiving broken JSON objects when going through our edge proxy that does chunked Transfer-Encoding.
anya: ugh. symptoms? partial lines, or event boundary misalign?
sam: likely chunk boundaries splitting a single SSE 'data' block into two TCP packets, proxy re-injects chunked frames with CRLFs. browsers' EventSource concatenates but our client lib parses per-
line and tries to JSON.parse each chunk -> fails.
michael: exactly. stacktrace from the client: 
```
Error: Unexpected end of JSON input
 at JSON.parse (<anonymous>)
 at parseSseChunk (widget-client.js:210)
```
tanisha: do we have telemetry showing how often SSE frames are partial vs full? Console shows increased parse errors starting ~08:15 UTC.
anya: console currently only counts socket disconnects and resume attempts, not per-chunk parse errors. we should avoid flooding logs with raw payloads though.
sam: quick fix idea: change client parser to buffer until it sees full event delimiter ("\n\n") before JSON.parse. low-risk and client-side.
michael: agreed as short-term. but root cause is our proxy doing Transfer-Encoding: chunked + adding its own chunk boundaries. that can also break our streaming parser in server-side consumers.
tanisha: longer term: add route-level flag to prefer "Connection: close" or to disable proxy chunking for SSE endpoints? that affects throughput and keepalive semantics though.
anya: routing policy tweak could be per-tenant flag in config. For Dedicated tenants we can pin a non-chunking passthrough. For hosted, need fallback.
sam: can we make the runtime emit SSE frames with explicit "event:" lines and small enough frames so proxies don't split inside a JSON blob? messy.
michael: also observed billing double-counts when client reconnects mid-event — metrics show resume attempts increment quota usage immediately, even if resume fails.
tanisha: that's bad for customers. we should gate billing increment until stream ACK (or after n bytes consumed). filing a ticket for quota gating.
anya: Can we add console telemetry tag to help differentiate proxy-induced fragmentation? propose tag: sse.proxy_fragment=true to attach to requests that had partial-chunk parses on server side.
michael: +1. Sam, can you prototype: 1) client buffer change, 2) server-side conservative parser, 3) console metric for fragment events.
sam: on it. I'll open a small PR for client buffer and runtime parser. PR will include unit tests for split-chunk events. ETA EOD.
deploy-bot: canary deployment scheduled: eng-runtime/canary/202/ -> 1 region at 2023-11-09T15:40Z.
tanisha: for rollout UX: add a quick checkbox in Console deploy wizard: "Preserve SSE framing (disable chunking)" so SEs can toggle per-route. low effort?
anya: depends on proxy infra. ops team would need a flag. I'll sync with infra.
michael: customer impacted is on hosted. Sam's client patch helps immediately. Tanisha, please prioritize quota-gating ticket P2 -> P1 for billing safety.
sam: PR: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/runtime/+/1234 — tests included, console events stubbed.
anya: adding telemetry ticket to backlog and assigning to me. will add dashboard panel: SSE parse errors by route + proxy hop.
tanisha: also notify support to pause automated billing adjustments for that tenant. ticket SENT to billing.
michael: thanks all. small follow-ups: - postmortem if we find proxy config root cause - add canary watch for parse errors metric during deployment - customer update draft?
anya: I'll draft customer note and share in #customer-success.
deploy-bot: canary completed: eng-runtime/canary/202/ -> success.
michael: monitor console for next hour and report. :eyes:
anya: initial telemetry looks promising — parse errors down after client patch on customer side. more verification next 30m.
